planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed in full sun on well-drained soil; the wide-spreading canopy benefits from a generous planting area and a warm, wind-sheltered site near a south wall on the Gulf Coast.

directions: Selected from seedling guavas on Oahu, Hawaii, Beaumont is a vigorous, wide-spreading tree bearing medium to large roundish fruit with pink, mildly acid, seedy flesh well suited to juice and processing as well as fresh eating. It is heavy-cropping and productive but somewhat more prone to fruit rots than tougher-skinned guavas, so good air circulation and prompt harvest of ripe fruit help limit losses in humid Gulf Coast summers. Guava trees are shallow-rooted and respond well to mulching and regular moisture, and should be protected from hard freezes with trunk wraps or overhead cover when young.
sources: California Rare Fruit Growers (CRFG) Fruit Facts: Guava

planting.note: Plant after last frost in full sun; this historic Florida selection crops heavily from late fall into early spring, so site it where winter fruit set can be monitored for cold protection.

directions: Developed in Florida as an improvement on the early 'Redland' guava, Supreme bears round fruit with thick, faintly aromatic white flesh, relatively few small seeds, and notably high vitamin C content. It is a heavy, extended cropper, setting fruit over roughly eight months from late fall through early spring in warm climates. On the Gulf Coast, grow in well-drained soil in full sun and protect young trees from frost, since bearing wood lost to cold delays the long fruiting season this cultivar is valued for.
sources: Julia Morton, Fruits of Warm Climates

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings after frost danger passes next to a sturdy post or trellis for the climbing cactus stems to grip; this self-pollinating selection sets fruit without hand pollination.

directions: Seoul Kitchen is a self-pollinating white-fleshed dragon fruit bearing medium, pink-skinned fruit with soft, creamy flesh, and it can flower and fruit in multiple cycles during a long warm season. The sprawling, three-angled cactus stems need a stout post, arbor, or trellis for support and benefit from occasional tip pruning to encourage branching and flowering. It tolerates heat and humidity well, making it a strong candidate for Gulf Coast gardens, but shallow aerial roots still need even moisture and excellent drainage to avoid stem rot. Protect from freezing temperatures with frost cloth or container culture where winters dip below the mid-30s.
sources: Growables.org Pitaya Species and Named Varieties

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings after frost danger passes along a sturdy post or trellis; fruit size improves with hand pollination even though the vine sets some fruit on its own.

directions: Zamorano is a deep-red-fleshed dragon fruit valued for its wine-like sweetness and medium to large fruit, often weighing over half a pound. The plant stays a manageable size, growing as a medium bush five to ten feet tall when supported, which makes it workable in home gardens or large containers. Give it full sun, sharply drained soil, and a strong post or trellis, and expect best fruit set and size with supplemental hand pollination of the night-blooming flowers. Protect from frost in winter, since Gulf Coast cold fronts below freezing can damage or kill unprotected stems.
sources: Growables.org Pitaya Species and Named Varieties

planting.note: Plant grafted trees after frost danger passes in full sun with excellent drainage; like other Israeli-bred atemoyas, hand pollination of the flowers improves fruit set and shape.

directions: Kabri is one of a group of atemoya cultivars selected in Israel from cherimoya x sugar apple crosses, grown for its sweet, custard-like white pulp and relatively smooth, pale green rind. As with most atemoyas, the flowers are poorly self-pollinated, so hand pollination in the early morning greatly improves fruit set, size, and shape. Give the tree full sun and well-drained soil, and shelter young plants from strong wind and salt spray near the Gulf Coast. Fruit should be picked when the skin begins to lighten and allowed to finish ripening at room temperature indoors.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Tropical Research and Education Center cultivar trials
California Rare Fruit Growers (CRFG) Fruit Facts: Atemoya

planting.note: Plant grafted trees after frost danger passes in full sun with excellent drainage; hand pollination of flowers improves fruit set as with other Israeli atemoya selections.

directions: Malali is another of the Israeli atemoya selections bred from cherimoya and sugar apple parentage, producing sweet, aromatic, custard-textured fruit with pale flesh and a thin, bumpy green rind. The tree is moderately compact compared to seedling sugar apples, and benefits from hand pollination of the short-lived flowers to improve fruit set and prevent lopsided fruit. Grow in full sun on well-drained soil, and protect from frost and strong coastal wind, since young wood is tender. Harvest when the fruit softens slightly and the segments begin to separate, then finish ripening at room temperature.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Tropical Research and Education Center cultivar trials
California Rare Fruit Growers (CRFG) Fruit Facts: Atemoya

planting.note: Plant grafted trees after frost danger passes in full sun with excellent drainage; this cultivar is noted for setting fruit without hand pollination, an advantage over many other atemoyas.

directions: Red Israel is an atemoya cultivar prized for its distinctive reddish, rough-scaled, heart-shaped fruit, which opens to reveal creamy white flesh that is sweet with a mildly tangy, berry-like note. Unlike many atemoyas it is productive without hand pollination, making it an easier choice for home growers. The tree is semi-deciduous and somewhat more frost-tolerant than true cherimoya, but still needs full sun, well-drained soil, and winter protection on the Gulf Coast. Harvest when the skin color deepens and the fruit yields slightly to gentle pressure, then ripen fully at room temperature before eating.
sources: California Rare Fruit Growers (CRFG) Fruit Facts: Atemoya

planting.note: Plant grafted trees after frost danger passes in full sun; this is one of the more cold-tolerant cherimoya cultivars, which helps on the subtropical Gulf Coast, but it still needs protection from hard freezes.

directions: Dr. White is a vigorous, fast-growing cherimoya cultivar bearing heart-shaped fruit with smooth-scaled, pale green to creamy-yellow skin and sweet, creamy custard-like flesh often compared to a blend of pineapple, banana, and papaya. It is regarded as one of the hardier cherimoya selections, tolerating light frost better than many others, which makes it a reasonable trial choice for sheltered Gulf Coast microclimates. Give it full sun, rich well-drained soil, and hand-pollinate flowers in the early morning to ensure good fruit set and avoid misshapen fruit. Harvest when the skin color lightens and the fruit gives slightly to pressure, then finish ripening indoors at room temperature.
sources: California Rare Fruit Growers (CRFG) Fruit Facts: Cherimoya

planting.note: Plant grafted or seed-grown trees after frost danger passes in full sun with excellent drainage; sugar apples are among the least cold-tolerant annonas and need full summer heat to fruit well.

directions: Big Red is a sugar apple selection notable for its vivid deep red to reddish-purple skin, a striking contrast to the typical pale green knobby fruit of the species, surrounding the same sweet, granular, custard-like white pulp. The small tree is naturally shrubby and well suited to a sunny Gulf Coast dooryard planting if given winter protection, since sugar apples are more cold-sensitive than atemoya or cherimoya. Hand pollination of the short-lived flowers in early morning greatly improves fruit set and size. Harvest when the segments on the fruit surface begin to separate slightly and the color deepens, then let it finish softening at room temperature.
sources: Julia Morton, Fruits of Warm Climates
